title: tri-sdk: lightweight reauth profiles, stream-sampler adapter, and parity ergonomics
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: tri-SDK users repeatedly asked for a small, explicit surface to express reauthentication windows and retry profiles while keeping streaming ergonomics consistent across Python/TS/Go. This PR introduces a lightweight ReauthProfile abstraction, a StreamSampler adapter to reduce noisy heartbeats for low-throughput real-time consumers, and alignment changes so Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs present the same defaults and helper names. Key goals: 1) reduce auth-related 401s during long-lived streams by adding configurable preemptive refresh windows; 2) offer pluggable retry presets that map to the platform's circuit/retry guidance; 3) provide a StreamSampler observer that suppresses frequent keepalive emissions for samplers marked as low-volume and aggregates telemetry into periodic hearts instead of per-chunk pings. Summary of changes: - Core: Add ReauthProfile (fields: refresh_window_ms, max_concurrent_refresh, jitter_ms) and surface helpers (from_env, from_static) implemented in tri-shared package. - SDK surfaces: Python: new ReauthProfile class, stream.sampler factory helper, refined AsyncIterator backpressure defaults. TypeScript: exported types and builder functions, added sampler decorator for ReadableStream consumers. Go: compact ReauthProfile struct, helper constructors, and a StreamSampler interface with default implementation. - Retries: introduce named retry presets (default, aggressive, conservative) and adapters to map to platform retry hints; SDKs now include telemetry tags for which preset was used. - Telemetry & CI: added unit + integration tests for reauth timing, sampler suppression tests, and smoke across all three SDKs; CI matrix added a flaky test tolerance entry. - Docs/Changelog: update quickstarts for streams to show reauth usage and sampler example; bump SDK versions: py 1.13.0 -> 1.14.0, ts 2.9.1 -> 2.10.0, go 0.8.4 -> 0.8.5. Backwards compatibility: all new APIs are additive; defaults preserve previous behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and approved in ENG-1459; - [x] Implementations in Python/TS/Go; - [x] Unit + integration tests; - [x] Docs and examples updated; - [x] Version bumps and changelog entries. Why unique: Combines an auth-window primitive with a streaming-specific sampler to address two correlated real-world pain points (auth drift on long streams and noisy keepalives) with a compact cross-SDK surface. Rollout plan: release SDKs in coordinated minor bumps, notify customers via changelog, enable new StreamSampler in a feature-flagged sample in the console for early adopters.
